newsitem.title: USA: Tosco Corp., union reach refinery labor pact.
newsitem.headline: Tosco Corp., union reach refinery labor pact.

text.p: Tosco Corp. and the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW) said Saturday they reached an agreement on a new five-year labour contract for four California refineries with about 1,400 workers.
Tosco is buying the four refineries from Unocal Corp. along with other related facilities in a $1.4 billion deal announced in November. Tosco said it expects to close the purchase on March 31.
The deal includes the Wilmington refinery, a nearby refinery in Carson, another in Rodeo east of San Francisco and one in Santa Maria, between Los Angeles and San Francisco.
Tosco's contract negotiations with the union had stalled last week, but company and union officials said on Monday that they had reached a tentative agreement.
On Saturday, Tosco and OCAW officials said the 900 union members at the four refineries had approved the contract.
"The membership did ratify the contract," Tosco spokeswoman Linda Saltzman said. "Production has been and will continue uninterrupted."
Union officials, who had threatened to strike, welcomed the agreement.

"We're looking forward to getting beyond this," said Howard Spencer, president of OCAW Local 1-326, which represents union members at the Rodeo plant east of San Francisco. "The contract was well accepted across the board."
Spencer said, however, that he and other union leaders were concerned by Tosco's plan to cut the workforce at the plants.

Tosco said it did not extend offers to an estimated 15 percent of the 1,400 Unocal employees at the four refineries and other facilities. Some of the workers accepted positions elsewhere within Unocal, accepted severance packages or retired early, Saltzman said.
Details of the new contract were not immediately available.
